title: feat(plugin-auth): no user-context restore of an API key revoked because its owner's membership ended
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-zhuang"} -->
_Requested by **Sam** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HP?thread=cmsg_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HPXGFhC5rGwDNXu4au6YC5H8)_

Closes #28387

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：`sys_api_key.revoked_reason` 新增一个取值 `organization_membership_ended`（与会话的 `revoke_reason` 同一个词）；带这个原因被撤销的 API 密钥，任何用户身份都不能通过 Restore 恢复，平台管理员也不行，服务端直接 403 并说明原因；被撤销密钥调用时的 `API_KEY_REVOKED` 提示也改为说明该密钥不可恢复。
- 为什么改：cloud 在成员被移出组织时会吊销他在各环境的密钥，但环境管理员可以用 Restore 把它恢复，等于把非成员的凭据重新打开。框架原先无法分辨这种吊销原因。
- 风险与回滚：只影响带这个新原因的密钥；`admin_password_reset` 的规则不变，系统上下文写入不受影响。框架自身不写这个原因，cloud 的写入在后续卡里做。回滚即撤销本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/api-key-restore-guard.ts`（规则 1，在读取管理员身份之前判定）、`packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts`（提示文字的新分支）、`packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-api-key.object.ts`（新选项与说明）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/api-key-restore-guard.test.ts src/forced-reset-revoke-reason-vocabulary.test.ts`，预期 24 个全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地（落地前席位做契约复核，其中一项偏离待裁定，见 Acceptance notes）。

## What changes

**The value.** `sys_api_key.revoked_reason` (`packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-api-key.object.ts`) gains the option `organization_membership_ended` ("Organization membership ended") beside `admin_password_reset`. It is the word `sys_session.revoke_reason` already carries when a membership removal ends a session (`MEMBERSHIP_ENDED_REVOKE_REASON`, plugin-auth `membership-ended-session.ts`), and the guard imports that same constant. The column stays readonly and off the ADR-0092 D2 whitelist. Its help text now names both reasons and who restores each; the six translated locales carry the new option and the new help, and the en bundle is regenerated (`check-i18n-bundles.mjs --write`). The platform never writes the value: a host that removes someone from the organization writes it in the system context, beside `revoked: true`.

**The refusal.** plugin-auth `api-key-restore-guard.ts` gains a rule judged before any standing is read: a user-context un-revoke of a row whose stored `revoked_reason` is `organization_membership_ended` is refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` whoever the caller is, on the by-id path and per row on a multi-row update. This is the server door the `restore_api_key` row action reaches (`PATCH /api/v1/data/sys_api_key/{id}`, `{ revoked: false }`); the action's `visible` is display only and is unchanged. The refusal says the owner's membership ended and that a member creates a new key (`POST /api/v1/keys`, or the API Keys page). Unchanged: the `admin_password_reset` rule and its message (byte-identical), the clear on every admitted restore, the reason kept on a re-revoke, and a system-context write is never refused, so a host can still re-admit a key and the reason clears.

**The key door's text.** `@objectstack/core` `lifecycleRefusalOf` (`packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts`) answered a revoked key with "Its owner or a platform administrator can restore it" for every reason but the forced reset. For a membership-ended key that is now false, so it gets its own arm: revoked because its owner's membership in the organization ended, cannot be restored, a member creates a new key. Code `API_KEY_REVOKED`, status 403 and every carried field are unchanged.

Changeset: `patch` for `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/core` (`Metadata-protocol: none`: the column is a system table's data value, not an authorable metadata key).

## Why

cloud#3403 (PR cloud#3423) revokes a removed member's keys in every environment, and named the follow-up: an environment administrator can restore such a key. The framework had no way to tell that revocation apart, because `revoked_reason` accepted only `admin_password_reset`. On a `single` deployment no per-request membership check refuses the key (the `organization_membership_ended` admission refusal in `resolve-authz-context.ts` runs only under a wall-enforcing posture), so the `revoked` flag is the only barrier, and anyone who could clear it reopened a non-member's credential.

## Tests

- **plugin-auth `api-key-restore-guard.test.ts`**, new top-level describe on the existing rig (real `ObjectQL` over SQLite, real `SecurityPlugin` with the shipped permission sets, the D2 guard, the guard under test, the real key door). Callers: the key's owner; a platform administrator by grant (`admin_full_access`, promoted by `bootstrapPlatformAdmin`); a platform administrator by the `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` anchor, with no grant row. Each admin case asserts `hasPlatformAdminStanding` first and ends with a control: the same caller restores a reset-revoked key, so the refusal is the reason's and not a caller who cannot reach the row. Also: the host's system write is stored with the reason; re-revoke and a smuggled `revoked_reason: null` keep it; an admin batch restore including such a key is refused whole; a system un-revoke lands and clears; the door text names no restorer.
- **plugin-auth `forced-reset-revoke-reason-vocabulary.test.ts`**: the option set is exactly the two values, and the new one equals the session word that `sys_session.revoke_reason` names.
- **core `api-key-lifecycle.test.ts`**: the membership-ended arm of the `API_KEY_REVOKED` text.
- **platform-objects `action-state-visibility.test.ts`**: Restore stays offered on a membership-ended row (the server decides).
- **dogfood `api-key-data-door-session-required.dogfood.test.ts`**, through the real HTTP door: the `restore_api_key` request read off the REGISTERED schema (method, target, `bodyExtra`), sent by the member's session and by the platform administrator's session, each refused 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, row unchanged, key still `API_KEY_REVOKED`; control: the administrator's same request restores a reset-revoked key (200, key works).
- Reason-only clear (seat review): a user-context write of `{ revoked_reason: null }` with no `revoked` key is refused 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` to the owner and both platform administrators (by grant and by the `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` anchor), on the engine and on the data door, so no restore follows it (head `a3727aaa`). The refuser is the ADR-0092 D2 guard; with the whitelist widened, the readonly strip still refuses it.

## Acceptance notes

- **Accepted-deviation candidate, for the contract review:** a platform administrator cannot restore a membership-ended key, unlike `admin_password_reset`, where they can. Reason: a non-member's key re-armed by anyone in a user context reopens the hole the revocation closed, and an environment's administrator is exactly the restorer cloud#3423 named. A system-context write still re-admits a key, so a host that re-adds the member can restore it deliberately. The admin-exemption alternative is measured below (it turns exactly the three admin legs red).
- Restore stays visible on such a row. The list views do not project `revoked_reason`, so a `visible` predicate on it would be unreliable; the server refusal says why.
- The cloud half is a separate card after a pin round: cloud's `environment-identity-revocation-plugin.ts` writes `revoked_reason: 'organization_membership_ended'` beside `revoked: true` for the `membership_ended` reason. Option membership is never enforced on a readonly select (objectql `record-validator.ts`, the open-vocabulary ruling), so that write would be stored even on today's pin; the refusal needs this release of plugin-auth.

## Verification

<details><summary>Ablations (each mutation landed on disk, run, restored to the HEAD blob)</summary>

- Rule 1 removed (`if (false && …)`), engine level: 5 of 19 red: owner, admin by grant, admin by email anchor, re-revoke, admin batch. Restored, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- Admin exemption added (the `admin_password_reset` pattern), engine level: 3 of 19 red: admin by grant, admin by email anchor, admin batch; the owner legs stay green.
- Admin exemption, HTTP level (plugin-auth rebuilt, marker proven in `dist/`, then the dogfood file): the platform administrator's leg red, `expected 200 to be 403`, the row restored and the reason cleared. Restore leg: rebuilt, marker proven absent from `dist/`, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- Core text arm removed: 1 of 23 red (the membership-ended text pin). Restored.

</details>

<details><summary>Local runs</summary>

All at head `eaefa983d` (objectstack-ai/objectstack), after the last commit.

- Package suites, under the verify lock: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` 240 files / 4257 passed, 10 skipped; `@objectstack/core` 136 / 3147 passed; `@objectstack/platform-objects` 120 / 1751 passed.
- `typecheck` (each package's own script, test-typecheck included): `core`, `platform-objects`, `plugin-auth`, `dogfood`, all Done.
- Dogfood, one file: `api-key-data-door-session-required.dogfood.test.ts` 10 / 10 passed (showcase closure built first). The full dogfood battery is not owed: no `!` in the title and no `(narrowing)` arm.
- `check:i18n` for platform-objects: in sync (20 bundles) after `--write`, which rewrote only the en bundle.
- `dispatch-gates --commands`: 75 families derived from the merge base `db5023141`; `--ran` reconciliation with recorded exit codes: 74 run with exit 0, 1 NOT MEASURED: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, PREREQUISITE NOT MET (exit 3; it reads every package's `dist/`, and only the plugin-auth, dogfood and cli closures were built here). CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` runs it on a full build.
- `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` first exited 3 because its positive-control fixture commit was outside this shallow clone; after fetching that one commit it passed (48 cases).
- Not run locally, owned by CI: the repo-wide `pnpm lint` and `test:repo`.

</details>

- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes (CI-owned run).

- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: not touched.
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
